display.title: Shiva Asar B'Tammuz: Five Sad Events
display.summary_short: Why we fast on the 17th of Tammuz: the five sad events that happened on that day, and our prayer that it soon become a day of joy.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given two days before the fast. Uncle Yossi explains that the 17th of Tammuz is a sad day in Jewish history, set aside for fasting, prayer and tzedakah, and lists the five sad things that happened on it: Moshe Rabbeinu came down from Har Sinai, saw the golden calf and broke the tablets; the daily offerings on the altar were stopped; the walls of Yerushalayim were breached by fire, leading to the destruction of the second Beis HaMikdash; the wicked Apostomos publicly burned a Sefer Torah; and an idol was placed in the Beis HaMikdash. We ask Hashem to send Moshiach, return us to Eretz Yisroel and rebuild the Beis HaMikdash, so that this sad day becomes a Yom Tov.
display.lesson: On the 17th of Tammuz we fast, pray and give tzedakah, and ask Hashem to turn the day into a Yom Tov with Moshiach.
